loads_at.description:
The precision this row loads at under the shared rule (`ml/native_dtype.py`), so a
client compares an artifact's precision with it without a second copy of the rule.
When the checkpoint's own dtype has not been read yet (`native_dtype` null) this is the
rule's default for the row — what the load itself does then — and `precision_note` says
it is a default. (This docstring said "None" there; the code never returned None.)
loads_at.title: Loads At

native_dtype.description: What the checkpoint's own config.json records (bfloat16, float16, float32), read from the file. With `quantization`, it decides what the model loads at.
native_dtype.title: Native Dtype

precision_note.description:
F-7 (2026-10-21): one sentence putting `quantization` and `loads_at` side by side.

A row listed `quantization: FP16` while its probe run recorded `model_dtype: bfloat16`,
and the two read as a contradiction. They are not: FP16 is the row's STORAGE FORMAT
(unquantized 16-bit weights, as opposed to Q8/Q4/Q2), and the 16-bit TYPE it runs in is
the checkpoint's own — bfloat16 for most current checkpoints.
precision_note.title: Precision Note

Use cases:
- Test synergistic effects (e.g., "formal" + "positive" = professional tone)
